indicator_definition: Healthy life years (HLY) at birth indicate the number of years a newborn is expected to live in good health, free from long-standing illness or disability. HLY are calculated by combining age-specific mortality rates with age-specific proportions of people reporting a limiting long-standing illness. The indicator is expressed in years and disaggregated by sex.
rationale: Healthy life years go beyond life expectancy by measuring the quality as well as the length of life. Increasing HLY means people not only live longer but spend more years in good health. Progress means a sustained increase in healthy life years for both men and women.
methodology_characteristics: HLY are calculated using the Sullivan method, combining mortality data with self-reported disability data from EU-SILC. The global activity limitation indicator (GALI) asks whether respondents have been limited in activities due to health problems for at least six months.
